text:
Maria: heads up — we had a partial telemetry drop this morning when the remote-config service flipped OTLP endpoints for all hosts at once. some exporters started spamming new endpoints, exhausted connections, and we saw transient 503s upstream.
Ashok: ow. any idea what remote-config sent? full endpoint list or a replace-all?
Maria: replace-all. config version bumped, and clients applied immediately. no splay/jitter.
Len: hmm, that's the problem. We need two things: (1) server-side staged rollout + percentage flag, (2) client-side splay/jitter and sticky primary endpoint with TTL.
Sophie: +1. Also add a small in-process circuit-breaker around the exporter so we stop hammering bad endpoints and let the cluster recover.
Ryan: agree. proposer: exporter should apply config like this:
```yaml
otlp_exporter:
  endpoints:
    - url: otlp-1.example.net:4317
    - url: otlp-2.example.net:4317
  primary_ttl_ms: 300000  # keep primary sticky for 5m
  splay_ms: 60000         # randomize apply over up to 60s
  circuit_breaker:
    request_limit: 50
    failure_threshold: 0.2
    cool_down_ms: 300000
  health_check_cmd: "grpc_health_probe -addr=%s -rpc-timeout=2s"
```
Maria: that looks good. we also need metrics exposed: exporter.endpoint.switches, circuit_breaker.trips, config.apply.latency. ops need these for dashboards.
Ashok: for HTTP fallback we should keep a separate backoff policy (shorter initial backoffs for HTTP because it's faster to recover) and prefer gRPC unless server advertises http-only.
Len: remote-config should also supply a rollout_id so clients can avoid re-applying the same logical change repeatedly (de-dupe).
Sophie: what about TTL for endpoint discovery? if DNS changes rapidly we shouldn't keep sticky primary too long. make primary_ttl configurable per env.
Ryan: +monitoring idea: emit a span when config received + another span when config applied. correlate with exporter errors to detect rollout regressions automatically.
Maria: ops asked for a safety-net: if exporter error-rate spikes > 5% across infra within 2m of a config change, auto-roll back to previous config. can we implement client-side reversion?
Ashok: yes, keep previous config in memory and reapply on rollback. but rollbacks must be splayed too.
Len: recommend a small server-side randomized cooldown too: remote-config rate-limit per client (e.g., at most 1 apply per 30s) to avoid tight loops.
Sophie: testing plan? we can run canary agents in prod group with 5% footprint and observe metrics for 15m before full rollout. add synthetic health-checks that exercise both gRPC and HTTP paths.
Ryan: also add a lightweight connpool drain: when switching primary, don't immediately close all idle conns; mark old conns draining for 30s to let in-flight streams finish.
Maria: sounds actionable. can we sketch a small implementation checklist?
Ashok: 1) client: config splay + primary_ttl + sticky selection + de-dupe by rollout_id.
Ashok: 2) client: circuit breaker + metrics + rollback to prev config.
Len: 3) remote-config: staged percentage rollout + per-client rate limits + rollout_id.
Sophie: 4) infra: dashboards + alerts (exporter error-rate, endpoint-switch-rate, circuit-breaker trips).
Ryan: 5) runtime: graceful conn drain + health-check probe + test harness for HTTP/gRPC fallback.
Maria: I'll open a short RFC and a ticket for the SDK changes. can someone pair on the remote-config side with me?
Len: I'll join. happy to take the remote-config staging piece.
Sophie: I'll own the circuit-breaker + metrics and the dashboard.
Ashok: I'll implement client apply logic + conn draining.
Ryan: I'll add the tracing spans + test harness.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for config-safety-net-test to 5% canary group (deploy id: cfg-2026-03-18-17). :white_check_mark:
Maria: thanks everyone. I'll paste the RFC link once it's up. :thumbsup:
